contributions.who: The Minister for School Standards (Georgia Gould)
contributions.text: Today I can confirm the publication of the provisional allocations for mainstream schools and local authorities through the schools and central school services national funding formulae as well as the high needs funding allocations for 2027-28. Our consultation response on up-front SEND funding for mainstream schools has also been published. Overall, the core schools budget in 2027-28 will total £66.7 billion. To simplify the funding system, allocations for mainstream schools, high needs and central school services will incorporate the additional funding provided in 2026-27 through the schools budget support grant 2026. This can be viewed online at: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/schools-budget-support-grant-2026-sbsg-26 As announced in July, those allocations will also incorporate a funding adjustment to reflect the reduction in employer contribution rates, for the teachers’ pension scheme from April 2027. The adjustment is available online at: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/teachers-pension-employer-contributions-funding-adjustment The reduction in pension contributions does not lead to a change in the value of teacher pensions or to a saving for the Gover
